sentences.text: Sooraj Saxena vs State Of Uttarakhand on 15 May, 2024

Author: Ravindra Maithani
Bench: Ravindra Maithani
High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 First Bail Application No.529 of 2024
Sooraj Saxena ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
Present:-
 Mr. Mani Kumar, Advocate for the applicant.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, Aga for the State.

Applicant Sooraj Saxena is in judicial custody in Fir No. 480 of 2023, dated 20.11.2023, under
Sections 363, 366, 376-A Ipc and Section 5/6 of The Protection Of Children From Sexual Offences
Act, 2012, Police Station Khatima, District Udham Singh Nagar.
He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the FIR, on 19.11.2023, at 07:30 in the evening, the victim, a young girl of 17 years left her house without informing anyone.
She revealed that she was in relationship with the applicant.
They wanted each other and on 19.11.2023, they left their houses and visited various places.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that there was a romantic relationship between the applicant and the victim; the age of the applicant is 24 years whereas, the victim is 17 years of age; it is argued that the victim has stated so, at every stage of investigation under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Conduct, 1973 ("the Code") and under Section 164 of the Code.
5. Learned State counsel admits these facts.

6. In the cases of Mahesh Kumar v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2023 SCC OnLine Del 2634, Faizan Wahid Baig v. The State of Maharashtra, MANU/MHOR/62774/2022, Vijaylakshmi and another v. State and another, 2021 SCC OnLine Mad 317, Shri John Franklin Shylla v. State of Meghalaya & Anr.,
2023 SCC OnLine Megh 303 and Ashik Ramjali Ansari v. State of Maharashtra and another, 2023 SCC OnLine Bom 1390, the Courts have either granted bail or quashed the proceedings or acquitted the accused in the cases like instant one.

sentences.text: Having considered, this Court is of the view that subject to certain conditions, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

9. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned, subject to the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant or any of his relatives shall not make any contact with the victim, in any manner, whatsoever, either physically, electronically or by any other means.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing the facts to court or any police officer and the applicant should not tamper with evidence.
(Ravindra Maithani, J) 15.05.2024 Sanjay Sooraj Saxena vs State Of Uttarakhand on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145004241/
